glosses: To include (something) as a part.

examples.text: The design of his house incorporates a spiral staircase.
to incorporate another's ideas into one's work
The Romans[…] did not subdue a country in order to put the inhabitants to fire and sword, but to incorporate them into their own community.

In spite of their small size and low weight, many technical developments which have proved themselves in main-line service have been incorporated, and a novelty in the 2-6-0-type is a tender cab to improve the conditions of tender-first running.

Firstly, a comprehensive and set-in-stone integrated timetable (incorporating trains, ferries, cable cars and buses, including the world-famous yellow 'post-autos'), compiled four years in advance and which gets tested twice before it becomes operational.

glosses: To mix (something in) as an ingredient; to blend

examples.text: Incorporate air into the mixture by whisking.

To form into a legal company.

examples.text: The company was incorporated in 1980.

glosses: To include (another clause or guarantee of the US constitution) as a part (of the Fourteenth Amendment, such that the clause binds not only the federal government but also state governments).
To form into a body; to combine, as different ingredients, into one consistent mass.

examples.text: By your leaves, you shall not stay alone, / Till holy church incorporate two in one.

glosses: To unite with a material body; to give a material form to; to embody.

examples.text: do not deny , that there was such an Opinion among the Heathens , that Spirits might possess Images , and be incorporated with them

glosses: Corporate; incorporated; made one body, or united in one body; associated; mixed together; combined; embodied.

And gazing on thee, sullen tree,

glosses: Not consisting of matter; not having a material body; incorporeal; spiritual.

examples.text: Moses forbore to speak of angels, and of things invisible, and incorporate.

The air vibrated at a white-hot temperature, the stones seemed to be trembling silently, ready to flow, and in the distance, at a curve of the road, the files of men, guns and horses seemed detached from the earth, and trembled like a mass of jelly in their onward progress, and it seemed to me that they were not living people that I saw before me, but an army of incorporate shadows.

glosses: An addition, an extension.

glosses: An appendix to a book or document.
An addition or extension to a building.
An addition to the territory of a country or state, from a neighbouring country or state, normally by military force.
To add something to another thing, especially territory; to incorporate.

examples.text: The ancient city of Petra was annexed by Rome.
In 1910, he returned to Korea, which had by this time been annexed by Japan.

glosses: To attach or connect, as a consequence, condition, etc.

examples.text: to annex a penalty to a prohibition, or punishment to guilt
Under Edward the Second, the Commons began to annex petitions to the bills by which they granted subsidies

Joindre une chose à une autre principale pour qu’elle en dépende.

glosses: Añadir algo (un anexo o apéndice; alguna información adicional, un territorio, una propiedad, etc.) a otra cosa de tal modo que se una y dependa de ella.
Unir algo a un envío, especialmente a una carta o mensaje electrónico.
Agregar un territorio o posesión a los ya existentes.

examples.text: Los primeros habitantes de Palau, fueron probablemente de Indonesia, poblaron las islas en el 1000 adC. El explorador español Ruy López de Villalobos avistó las islas en 1543 y las anexionó al Imperio Español.
Aprovechando que los bereberes habían abandonado la zona noroeste de la península, se anexionó Galicia en el 740.
Brevemente como un protectorado, el mandato del Reino Unido fue traspasado en 1901 cuando Nueva Zelanda anexionó la isla.
Fernando I de Castilla se anexionó la comarca para su reino castellano que era hasta ese momento territorio navarro.
El primero se anexionó a principios del siglo XX mientras que los otros ya estaban incluidos antes.
La URSS se anexionó Besarabia al comienzo de la II Guerra Mundial (véase Pacto Molotov-Ribbentrop) y de nuevo al final del conflicto, reorganizándola como la RSS de Moldavia.
